places.w: Taiwan's capital, a relaxed city of night markets, temples and green hills.
places.y: Some of Asia's best street food, an MRT that goes everywhere, and hot springs and volcano hikes inside the city limits.
places.l: North Taiwan; the airport (TPE) is 40 min away by Airport MRT.

places.w: One of Taipei's oldest night markets: a single long lane of stalls.
places.y: Famous for black-pepper buns baked in a clay oven at the entrance; easier to walk than Shilin.
places.l: Songshan, east Taipei, next to MRT Songshan.

places.w: A volcanic national park on Taipei's northern edge.
places.y: Steaming fumaroles, silver-grass slopes in autumn, hot springs and the city's highest peaks.
places.l: About 50 min from central Taipei: MRT to Jiantan, then a bus up.

places.w: Taipei's highest peak (1,120 m), a dormant volcano in Yangmingshan.
places.y: A short, steep climb past sulphur vents to views over the city and the north coast.
places.l: Yangmingshan; the usual start is the Xiaoyoukeng trailhead.

places.w: A fumarole field and trailhead on the side of Qixingshan.
places.y: Hissing yellow sulphur vents right beside the path.
places.l: Yangmingshan, by bus from MRT Jiantan.

places.w: Taipei's hot-spring district.
places.y: Public outdoor baths, the steaming Thermal Valley and a Japanese-era bathhouse museum.
places.l: North Taipei, about 30 min by MRT from Taipei Main (Xinbeitou station).

places.w: A steaming jade-green sulphur lake, also called Hell Valley.
places.y: Clouds of hot vapour drifting over the water.
places.l: Beitou, a 10-min walk from MRT Xinbeitou.

places.w: Taipei's biggest and best-known night market.
places.y: Giant fried chicken, oyster omelettes and a maze of food stalls.
places.l: Shilin, north Taipei, by MRT Jiantan.

places.w: Taipei's 19th-century merchant quarter along Dihua Street.
places.y: Tea and dried-goods shops, restored shophouses turned into cafés, sunsets over the river.
places.l: West Taipei by the Tamsui river, near MRT Beimen.

places.w: Taipei's most famous breakfast counter.
places.y: Thick egg flatbread from a clay oven and warm soy milk; the queue moves fast.
places.l: Upstairs in Huashan market, next to MRT Shandao Temple.

places.w: Tea-growing hills on Taipei's southern edge.
places.y: A gondola over the forest, tea houses with the city below, cooler air.
places.l: Wenshan, south Taipei; gondola from MRT Taipei Zoo (about 25 min ride).

places.w: A small hill with a steep stair trail (Xiangshan).
places.y: The classic view of Taipei 101, best at sunset.
places.l: Xinyi, east Taipei, from MRT Xiangshan.

places.w: Taipei's 508 m landmark skyscraper.
places.y: Best seen from Elephant Mountain; observation deck on the 89th floor.

places.w: A neighbourhood night market (also called Tonghua).
places.y: Smaller and more local than Shilin, good cheap snacks.
places.l: Da'an, near MRT Xinyi Anhe, 15 min from Elephant Mountain.

places.w: A riverside area where the Keelung and Tamsui rivers meet.
places.y: Start of the flat riverside bike path to Tamsui; wetlands and birds.

places.w: A riverside town at the mouth of the Tamsui river.
places.y: Old-street snacks, colonial forts and Taipei's best sunsets over the water.
places.l: End of the red MRT line, about 40 min from Taipei Main.

places.w: A red fort first built by the Spanish (1628), later rebuilt by the Dutch and used as the British consulate.
places.y: Small, pretty and full of history, with a view over the river mouth.
places.l: Tamsui, 15 min on foot from the MRT.

places.w: A quiet district across the river from Tamsui (not the Indonesian island).
places.y: Flat riverside bike path and lawns, reached by a 10-min ferry.
places.l: Opposite Tamsui; ferry from Tamsui pier.

places.w: Tamsui's old fishing harbour with a white footbridge.
places.y: The sunset spot at the river mouth.
places.l: North end of Tamsui, by bus, bike or boat from the old street.

places.w: Taipei's busy youth and shopping district.
places.y: Pedestrian streets, street food and cheap eats until late.

places.w: A small rail junction town.
places.y: Where you change for the Jiufen bus and the Pingxi branch line.
places.l: North-east coast, about 45 min by train from Taipei Main.

places.w: A former gold-mining town on a steep hillside above the sea.
places.y: Narrow lanes, old tea houses and red lanterns; magical once the day-trippers leave.
places.l: North-east coast, about 1h from Taipei (train to Ruifang, then 15 min by bus).

places.w: A former gold-mining village with the Gold Museum and Japanese-era houses.
places.y: Quieter than Jiufen; the start of the Teapot Mountain trail.
places.l: 10 min by bus (or 40 min on foot) beyond Jiufen.

places.w: A rocky ridge shaped like a teapot above Jinguashi.

places.l: Above Jinguashi; trailhead behind the Gold Museum.

places.w: A waterfall stained gold by minerals from the old mines.
places.y: Strange colours, an easy roadside stop.
places.l: On the road from Jinguashi down to the coast.

places.w: A bay where mineral runoff turns the water yellow against the blue sea.
places.y: A striking two-colour sea seen from the coast road.
places.l: Below Jinguashi, on the coast at Shuinandong.

places.w: A little single-track railway up a forested valley of old coal towns.
places.y: Sky lanterns, waterfalls and trains rolling right through village streets.
places.l: Branches off at Ruifang; Shifen is 30 min down the line.

places.w: A village on the Pingxi line, famous for sky lanterns.
places.y: The train runs down the main street; Shifen waterfall is a 20-min walk.
places.l: Pingxi line, about 30 min from Ruifang.

places.w: The quiet end of the Pingxi line, an old coal-mining stop.
places.y: A wooden station and a little old street, calmer than Shifen.
places.l: End of the Pingxi line, about 15 min past Shifen.

places.w: A coastal district on Taiwan's north coast.
places.y: Tandem paragliding launches from the hill above the sea.
places.l: North coast, about 1h by bus from Taipei.

places.w: A cape of wind- and sea-carved rocks.
places.y: Mushroom rocks and the famous 'Queen's Head'.
places.l: Wanli, north coast, about 1h by bus from Taipei.

places.w: A port city north-east of Taipei.
places.y: Miaokou night market's seafood.
places.l: About 45 min by train from Taipei Main.

places.w: Keelung's famous seafood night market around an old temple.
places.y: Crab, oysters and tempura, lanterns overhead.
places.l: Central Keelung, a 10-min walk from the station.

places.w: The main town on Taiwan's east coast, between steep mountains and the Pacific.
places.y: Gateway to Taroko gorge, seaside bike paths and Indigenous food.
places.l: East coast, about 2h15 by train from Taipei.

places.w: A long crescent of pebble beach.
places.y: Wide Pacific views at the end of a flat seaside bike path.
places.l: About 10 km north of Hualien town.

places.w: Hualien's big night market.
places.y: An Indigenous food street with grilled meats, plus local snacks.
places.l: Central Hualien, walkable from most guesthouses.

places.w: Old winery buildings turned into a creative park.
places.y: Cafés, small shops and exhibitions; good on a rainy day.

places.w: A marble gorge national park, Taiwan's most famous.
places.y: Sheer marble walls and a turquoise river; only parts are open since the 2024 earthquake.
places.l: About 30 min north of Hualien by taxi.

places.w: A village and rest area deep inside Taroko gorge.
places.y: Temples, a suspension bridge and short walks, when the road is open.
places.l: About 1h up the gorge from Hualien.

places.w: A short stair trail in Taroko.
places.y: A steep climb through forest to views over the gorge mouth.

places.w: Sea cliffs that drop about 1,000 m straight into the Pacific.
places.y: One of Taiwan's most dramatic coastal views.
places.l: North of the Taroko entrance, about 40 min from Hualien.

places.w: Hualien's museum of marble and stone carving.
places.y: A dry plan B near the sea.

places.w: A Rift Valley village known for iron-rich hot springs.
places.y: Rust-coloured, slightly salty water; quiet baths.
places.l: About 1h south of Hualien by train.

places.w: Hualien's largest lake, ringed by forested hills.
places.y: A flat 5 km bike loop round the water.
places.l: About 40 min by bus south-west of Hualien.

places.w: A 1940s Japanese army headquarters in a grove of old pines.
places.y: A shady terrace, a café and views over Hualien harbour.
places.l: A hill above Hualien port, walkable from town.

places.w: A small coastal village with a big hillside temple.
places.y: The south end of the Caoling Historic Trail.
places.l: North-east coast (Yilan), about 1h from Jiufen by bus and train.

places.w: A Qing-dynasty path over grassy coastal hills.
places.y: Silver grass, grazing cattle and the Pacific below you for hours.
places.l: North-east coast, between Dali and the Fulong area.

places.w: A long golden-sand beach.
places.y: The end point of the Caoling trail; a swim and the train back.
places.l: Gongliao, north-east coast, about 1h by train from Taipei.

places.w: A rocky headland with a cliff-top trail and a lighthouse.
places.y: A short, windswept loop with big sea views.
places.l: North-east coast, between Jiufen and Fulong.

places.w: A valley of turquoise pools in Truku Indigenous land.
places.y: Suspension bridges and a clear river through a small gorge; a free permit is needed.
places.l: About 40 min by taxi north-west of Hualien.

places.w: Taipei's best-known temple, founded in 1738.
places.y: Carved dragons, incense and worshippers day and night.
places.l: Wanhua, west Taipei, MRT Longshan Temple.

places.w: A richly decorated folk temple, restored with a UNESCO award.
places.y: Some of the finest temple carving and painting in Taiwan.
places.l: Datong, north-west Taipei, near MRT Yuanshan.

places.w: A rice-growing plain on the north-east coast.
places.y: Where the train first meets the sea on the way to Hualien.
places.l: North-east Taiwan, about 1h by train from Taipei.

places.w: Taiwan's big southern port city.
places.y: Harbour art districts, Cijin island seafood, a relaxed feel.
places.l: South-west Taiwan; the airport (KHH) is 30 min away by MRT.

places.w: Taiwan's oldest city and former capital.
places.y: The island's food capital, hundreds of temples and old lanes.
places.l: South-west Taiwan, 12 min by high-speed train from Kaohsiung (Zuoying).

places.w: Taiwan's first Confucian temple, founded in 1665.
places.y: Quiet red courtyards under old banyans.

places.w: A temple to the sea goddess Mazu, in a former Ming prince's residence.
places.y: One of Tainan's most beautiful temples.

places.w: A short lane of old wooden houses by the old canal.
places.y: Lanterns, small bars and shops; lovely at night.
places.l: West Tainan, 10 min on foot from the centre.

places.w: Tainan's old harbour district.
places.y: The Dutch Fort Zeelandia (1624), the Tree House and snack streets.
places.l: About 5 km west of central Tainan: bike or bus.

places.w: An old trading warehouse swallowed by banyan roots.
places.y: Walkways through the roots and branches; eerie and beautiful.
places.l: Anping, next to the old Tait & Co. building.

places.w: Tainan's biggest night market (Thu, Sat, Sun).
places.y: Hundreds of stalls on a huge lot.
places.l: North Tainan, a short taxi ride from the centre.

places.w: A 1653 Dutch fort (Provintia), rebuilt with Chinese pavilions.
places.y: A pretty courtyard with stone turtles; a Tainan symbol.

places.w: A 1932 department store from the Japanese era, restored.
places.y: An old lift, Taiwanese crafts and a rooftop shrine.

places.w: Tainan's long beach promenade.
places.y: Sunset over the Taiwan Strait.
places.l: South-west of Anping, about 25 min by bus from the centre.

places.w: A Tainan night market (Mon, Tue, Fri).
places.y: Local and less touristy.

places.w: A mangrove area with a 'green tunnel' boat ride.
places.y: A narrow canal under arching mangroves.
places.l: North of Anping, about 30 min by bus from central Tainan.

places.w: A short forest path at the water's edge.

places.w: The tea township next to Sun Moon Lake.
places.y: Taiwan's famous black (Assam) tea and the tea research station.

places.w: The highest peak around Sun Moon Lake (2,059 m).
places.y: A long, steep forest climb to a view over the whole lake.
places.l: Trailhead 15 min by taxi from Shuishe.

places.w: A short trail through tea plantations.
places.y: An easy hour among tea bushes and forest.
places.l: By the Yuchi tea research station.

places.y: Start of the Alishan Forest Railway; famous turkey rice.
places.l: About 50 min by train north of Tainan.

places.y: Giant ancient cypresses, sunrise over a sea of clouds, high-mountain tea.
places.l: About 2h30 by forest railway from Chiayi.

places.w: Alishan's sunrise viewpoint (about 2,490 m).

places.w: A steep stair trail to cliffs on Tashan.
places.y: Views over a sea of clouds and deep valleys.

places.w: A giant cypress said to be about 2,700 years old.
places.y: A quiet walk along an old logging rail line.

places.w: A high pass at the edge of Yushan National Park (about 2,600 m).

places.w: An easy peak (2,845 m) near Tataka.
places.y: Big views of Yushan for little effort.

places.w: Taiwan's highest mountain (3,952 m).
